extracted.intended_audience: journal peer reviewers (researchers asked to review manuscripts for PLOS or similar journals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and writing a peer review of a journal manuscript, including structure, substantive critique, tone, and procedural notes for recommendations and confidential comments to editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review structure (inverted pyramid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the report like an 'inverted pyramid' with the most critical information first, followed by details and then supplementary points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a concise overview (critical points and recommendation), then provide specific improvements (major then minor), and finish with any additional or ancillary observations. This ordering helps editors quickly see key judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary section — restate manuscript claims and recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin by restating the manuscript's claims in your own words and provide an overview of strengths and weaknesses, concluding with your recommendation (accept, revise, reject).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restating claims demonstrates understanding and helps reveal perspective differences among reviewers; keep this section concise and focused on the central contributions and shortcomings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific improvements — divide into major and minor issues; number points
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide feedback into major and minor issues and number each point for clarity; reference specific lines, pages, figures, or tables when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbering helps authors and editors address items; always point to exact locations (line/page/figure/table) so authors can act on feedback efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Major issues are essential points that must be resolved before publication and concern foundational aspects of the current study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on problems that affect the manuscript's validity, interpretation, or principal conclusions; avoid turning major issues into requests for future or out-of-scope experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor issues are problems that do not affect the overall conclusions and include items like missing references, technical clarifications, data presentation/formatting, and grammar/spelling corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List minor items clearly and succinctly; these are actionable fixes that improve clarity or presentation but do not change the study's substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate section for confidential concerns about ethics, language quality, or competing interests that the editor should know; not for critiquing the manuscript itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use this space to critique the manuscript because editors will not share it with authors; limit content to issues that require editorial discretion (e.g., suspected misconduct, serious ethical issues, undisclosed conflicts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify recommendations with concrete evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Support your recommendation (accept/revise/reject) with concrete evidence drawn from the manuscript and your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why you reached a decision using specific examples, data, or methodological concerns rather than vague assertions; this helps editors and authors understand the basis of your judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific about needed improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific, actionable instructions for what authors should change or clarify to address issues you raise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague suggestions; indicate precisely what analyses, clarifications, or rewrites are necessary and where they should be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a professional, respectful tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Use professional and respectful language throughout the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transform blunt or insulting comments into constructive critique (example: replace 'The authors appear clueless' with 'The study fails to address how findings relate to previous research'); respectful tone increases likelihood authors will engage productively with feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge manuscript strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly note the manuscript's strengths alongside weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing criticism with acknowledgement of positive aspects improves fairness and helps editors weigh the manuscript's overall contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not suggest out-of-scope experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid requesting experiments or analyses that are beyond the scope of the current study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on what is necessary to validate the manuscript's claims rather than proposing extensive new work that would constitute a new project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rewrite the manuscript for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rewrite text or re-author large parts of the manuscript for the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide guidance and indicate where improvements are needed, but do not undertake to redraft large sections; reviewers should point out problems and suggest solutions, not perform the revision themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not promote your own research
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using the review to promote your own work or unduly favor your publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure citations or suggestions that reference your work are relevant and justified; disclose any competing interests as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not focus excessively on typos
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid giving disproportionate weight to minor typographical errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While clarity and presentation matter, do not let trivial formatting or punctuation issues dominate the review; note them as minor fixes rather than central criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread your review before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit the review without proofreading it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the review is clear, free of careless mistakes, and professionally presented—this improves readability and credibility with editors and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transform vague criticism into constructive feedback (tone guideline)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a critique risks being vague or insulting, rephrase it to explain the specific shortcoming and how it could be remedied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide example phrasings and concrete alternatives; this makes feedback actionable and less adversarial (see example in guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of review submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit reviews on time to maintain good standing with editors and increase chances of future review invitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting deadlines builds editor relationships; if delayed, communicate with the journal promptly to request more time.
